thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — High latency + error spike detected for service=vector-search-euc1 (5m p95 latency > 2.1s and error rate ~9%). Paging @maria (oncall). Alert: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/1839001234

maria: Ack. I'm looking. First pass: a lot of 502s coming from model-cache-proxy when fetching shards, and CPU on nodes running vector-search jumped. Rolling tailing logs now.

maria: Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n inference top pods -l app=vector-search --containers
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-cache-proxy --tail=300 | grep -i "econnrefused\|timeout\|cache miss"
kubectl -n inference get nodes -o wide | grep euc1
```

rob: Noted. Yesterday there was a maintenance window that replaced one NFS server (hosted by infra) — could be higher cache miss rate causing more model downloads. I'll ping infra on-call.

jin: Support here. Which customers should we notify right away? Any accounts running long vector jobs in eu-central? I'll draft macros.

maria: Impact: partial failures and high latency for vector-search in EU-Central-1. Roughly 7-10% of API calls impacted in last 8m. Top affected accounts (based on recent requests): data-alpha, searchlabs, analytics-inc. No sign of index corruption; likely cache/backing store saturation.

rob: infra-oncall (tagging @olivia): could NFS throughput be the bottleneck? If so, quick mitigation might be to serve models from local SSD on hot nodes or throttle background prefetch.

olivia: Infra here — confirmed NFS server in eu-c has elevated I/O wait since 30m ago and a degenerate GC loop on the storage controller. We are restarting the controller now, ETA 10m. Meanwhile, consider reducing model fetch concurrency on model-cache-proxy.

maria: From runtime side we can set an env var to reduce parallel fetches: MODEL_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=4 (default 16). That should reduce contention. I'll apply as a canary to two pods first.

jin: Drafting customer-facing language now. Short Zendesk macro for high-level notice:
```
We are investigating intermittent timeouts and increased latency for the Vector Search API in EU-Central-1. Our engineers are actively mitigating and we expect to provide a follow-up within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.
```

jin: Detailed Zendesk macro (for escalations):
```
Summary: Elevated error rates and p95 latency for Vector Search in EU-Central-1 due to model-cache backend saturation.
Current status: Teams are applying a mitigation (reducing model fetch concurrency and restarting a storage controller) and monitoring for improvement.
Impact: Partial request failures and higher latency for vector-search requests in eu-central. No data loss observed.
Workarounds: If feasible, please retry failed requests after a short backoff. For customers running large bulk indexing jobs, consider pausing until we confirm recovery.
Next update: within 30 minutes. For urgent concerns, reply with your account id.
```

jin: Intercom snippet (copy):
```
Quick update: We're investigating increased latency and intermittent errors for Vector Search in EU-Central-1. Engineers are applying mitigations and we'll update shortly (within 30 minutes). Sorry for the disruption.
```

maria: Internal ops post for eng-sre (short):
```
INVESTIGATING: vector-search-euc1 -> model-cache I/O saturation after storage controller GC. Symptoms: p95++ and ~9% 5xx. Mitigation in-flight: reduce MODEL_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY to 4 on canary pods, restart controller (infra). If that fails: consider temporary rate-limit on vector-search or switch hot nodes to local-ssd-backed copies. @olivia keep us posted on controller restart.
```

cs-bot: Note — when posting to statuspage set impact to "Partial outage" and affected component: Vector Search (eu-central-1). Tag severity: major.

rob: Runbook reference: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/vector-search-cache-and-storage. Steps 2-4 cover prefetch tuning + fallback to local ssd.

maria: Applying canary now (commands):
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/vector-search MODEL_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=4 --record
# patch only canary label set
kubectl -n inference patch deployment vector-search -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"canary":"true"}}}}}'
```

olivia: Storage controller restart complete. Observed immediate drop in I/O wait, but still watching for downstream recovery.

maria: Canary shows p95 drop from 2.3s -> 1.1s and 5xx rate down to 2% on those pods. Good sign. Rolling the concurrency change to remaining pods with 3m canary window.

jin: I'll push Zendesk short macro to affected open tickets and tag priority accounts for proactive outreach. Preparing follow-up template for "Mitigated" with remediation notes and FAQs.

maria: Handoff checklist if someone else takes over: paste latest checks (canary results + commands run), current error rate, and whether infra confirmed storage controller healthy. Keep CS notified every 30 min until resolved.

rob: If we need a rollback-style action, we can also toggle PREFETCH_FEATURE_FLAG off to force older behavior: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/vector-search PREFETCH_FEATURE_FLAG=false`. Use canary and watch.

olivia: Confirming storage controller GC root cause and filing ticket with infra storage team for follow-on fix.

jin: Statuspage copy suggestions:
- Investigating: "We are investigating elevated latency and errors for Vector Search in EU-Central-1."
- Identified: "We have identified storage controller I/O saturation causing increased model fetch latency. Mitigation being applied."
- Mitigated: "Mitigation applied (reduced model fetch concurrency and controller restart). Systems recovering, monitoring in progress."
- Resolved: "Issue resolved. Service restored. Postmortem to follow."

maria: Taking a short break but monitoring alerts. If anyone takes over, post "taking over" and include the last observed p95 and 5xx numbers. Back at ~1839002100.

jin: Proactive note to CS: I've queued Intercom messages for impacted customers and will update tickets once rolling change completes.

maria: (reacts with :thumbsup:) — thanks team. Leaving key commands and canary metrics in this thread for the next oncall.
